name: split a pile into three by a rule you chose
one_line: A pile of unlike things, three piles to make of them, and the rule for dividing them is written by whoever divides.
how: List eleven small things that could have come out of one box: a bone button, a key with no lock, half a photograph, a string knotted three times, a bent coin. Print three lines, «first pile: the ones that ___», and nothing more, because the rule is theirs. Close the easy road inside the instruction and by name — «and it may not be big, medium and small» — since a ban costs one line and three lines of encouragement buy nothing. Three piles and not two: two is a true-or-false with a heap on each side. Last line: one of the eleven sits in two piles at once, ring it.

knobs.effect: Given by whoever printed the sheet, it is a multiple-choice question spread over eleven items and can be got wrong; chosen by whoever sorts, nothing can be wrong and the mental work is unchanged.
Two is a yes and a no and inherits everything wrong with true or false; three or more force a look at the objects instead of at the question, which is where the sorting starts.

knobs.knob: whether everything has to be placed
knobs.effect: With a pile for everything the sorting comes out tidy and nobody hesitates; with a fourth pile allowed for «I do not know», that pile is usually where the interesting objects end up.
One rule reads as the rule; a second pass with a different one shows that the first was one of many, which is the point of the form and costs a single line.

where_the_work_is: In the eleven objects. They have to resist the obvious cuts, which means listing things that share nothing and putting in at least one that honestly belongs in two piles.
breaks: Only the three written rules come back, and a rule that reads well sits just as comfortably over a pile sorted at random; the sheet cannot tell. Real objects work better than a printed list, and then nothing of the sorting survives on paper at all. Eleven names fit on a display; the three lines to write on do not.
